title: Identity-normalized shift and distinguished-triangle compatibility of specialization
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and any scheme $Y$ with no structure map to $k$; its universe is independent of that of $\Omega$. Let $I$ be the directed finite coefficient subfields [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. On the fixed intrinsic rational stages $C_E=\mathrm{sfRationalConstructibleCategory}(\ell,\mathrm{Shrink}(E),Y)$, obtained by raw rationalization of the intrinsic integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], let $S$ and $S_D$ be the normalized scalar systems with proof parameters $0$ and $p$, respectively [lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages]. Use the equality $\eta:S=S_D$ of [lem-pur-general-specialization-pairs], and set $P=S.\mathrm{PairCategory}$, $P_D=S_D.\mathrm{PairCategory}$ [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Let $e:P\simeq P_D$ be equality transport, namely $\mathrm{Pi.eqToEquivalence}(T\mapsto T.\mathrm{PairCategory},\eta)$; this specifies the functor, not an arbitrary equivalence.

Use the representative identifications of [lem-pur-general-specialization-pairs] and the prescribed additive Hom structures of [lem-pur-general-specialization-hom-additivity]. Equip $P$ with the uniquely normalized shifts and compatible stage identifications of [lem-pur-general-pair-shift-normalization, lem-pur-general-transition-shift-compatibility], and $P_D$ with those of [lem-pur-general-intrinsic-finite-field-transport]. There is exactly one coherent integer-shift comparison $c_n:e(A[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}e(A)[n]$ whose hom component at every $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $A\in P$ is the identity of the displayed shifted pair, after the prescribed object equalities. For the common-stage Verdier pretriangulations [lem-route-common-stage-verdier-exists-unique, def-weil-triangulated-category], $e$ with this fixed comparison preserves and reflects distinguished triangles:
$$V\text{ is distinguished in }P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad e^\triangle(V)\text{ is distinguished in }P_D.$$
In particular $e$ is exact for this comparison. A supplied common-stage cone keeps its finite coefficient label, its literal third pair $(L,C)$ and all three specified arrows, including the connecting arrow.

source.note: Construction material retained from the former supporting proof final step. The two normalized scalar shift comparisons coincide by the existing stage theorem and the integral/rational uniqueness specifications, rather than by an arbitrary ofIso choice. The representative shift formulas therefore agree under eta. Identity hom components on shifted pairs are natural by specialization_pairs and that representative formula. The shift-zero and shift-add equations agree componentwise by the identity inclusion normalizations. Thus these components give a coherent CommShift structure. Natural-isomorphism extensionality and proof irrelevance make it unique. Every distinguished triangle is isomorphic to a distinguished finite-stage image. Equality transport fixes the finite triangle and its first two arrows; the identity shift comparison fixes its connecting arrow. Map its witnessing triangle isomorphism to obtain preservation. Apply the inverse equality transport to obtain reflection, keeping the inverse identity-normalized comparison. The forward implication is precisely specialization_exact. For the literal cone, conjugate the stage image by isoToStage at the first two objects and the identity at the third; the first square is mkHom_eq_isoToStage, the second a unit equation, the third cancels the shifted inverse identification. Old cone argument 4 and intrinsic cone argument 13 are retained in the cone and intrinsic nodes as well.

proof.text: Identify $S$ and $S_D$ using $\eta$, with the pair and representative equalities specified by lem-pur-general-specialization-pairs. Parameter independence in lem-general-algebraically-closed-coefficient-stages identifies the prescribed coherent transition comparisons $\sigma_{EL,n}$ as well as the scalar functors; this uses their integral-image normalization, not an arbitrary comparison. The Hom-coordinate and additivity equalities of lem-pur-general-specialization-hom-additivity identify the already prescribed Hom group operations under the same equality transport. Consequently both constructions now use the same fixed category, group laws, stage shifts and transition comparisons. Equality induction on $\eta$ makes the specified $e$ the identity functor on this common category.

proof.text: Pull the prescribed shift structure on $P_D$ back through the equality of step 1. By lem-pur-general-intrinsic-finite-field-transport it has object formula $(E,K)[n]=(E,K[n])$, representative formula $[L,u]\mapsto[L,\sigma_{FL,n,H}^{-1}\circ u[n]\circ\sigma_{EL,n,K}]$, additive shift functors, and coherent inclusion comparisons with identity components. These are exactly the specification of lem-pur-general-pair-shift-normalization on the fixed category and Hom groups. Its uniqueness identifies this transported structure with the prescribed one on $P$, including the shift-zero and shift-add isomorphisms. The inclusion comparisons also agree: their hom components are the specified identities, their inverse components are determined by the inverse laws, and their coherence fields are proofs.

proof.text: In the equal-category, equal-shift situation of step 2, take $c_{n,A}=1_{A[n]}$ with inverse the same identity. Naturality is $f[n]\circ1=1\circ f[n]$. The shift-zero comparison is the composite of a shift-zero isomorphism with its inverse, and the shift-add comparison is the composite of the same shift-add isomorphism with its inverse, so both coherence equations hold. Transport back along $\eta$ to obtain the required coherent comparison for the specified $e$. Any other normalized comparison has the same hom component at every $n,A$; inverse laws determine its inverse components. Thus its natural isomorphisms agree componentwise, and its coherence proofs agree by proof irrelevance. This proves existence and uniqueness without changing the comparison.

proof.text:
Use the supplied exact-stage pair data. Their canonical stage identifications have the required shift compatibility on $P$ by lem-pur-general-transition-shift-compatibility and on $P_D$ by lem-pur-general-intrinsic-finite-field-transport. The common-stage Verdier theorem identifies distinguishedness with $D_S$ and $D_{S_D}$ for these fixed data. By def-sf-directed-common-stage-data, a witness is a finite label $L$, a distinguished triangle $U=(x\xrightarrow f y\xrightarrow g z\xrightarrow h x[1])$ in the same $C_L$, and an isomorphism $V\cong j_L^\triangle U$. In the coordinates of steps 1-3, the image of its third arrow is
$$c_{1,j_Lx}\circ e(\beta_{L,1,x}\circ j_Lh)=\beta^D_{L,1,x}\circ j_L^Dh;$$
the first two arrows are likewise unchanged. Triangle isomorphisms have three component maps and three commuting squares; with the equal shifts all three squares and the inverse component maps are unchanged. Thus precisely the same $L,U$ and isomorphism witness $D_S(V)$ and $D_{S_D}(e^\triangle V)$ in either direction. The two common-stage criteria give the required equivalence of distinguishedness.

proof.text: For a supplied common-stage cone, apply the preceding identifications to its actual three arrows. Every arrow has a finite representative, and specialization_pairs keeps that label and finite map. The literal third object $(L,C)$ is fixed by the pair equality. The first and second arrows are their same representatives, and the third becomes $c_{1,A}\circ e(h)=e(h)$ in the displayed equal-shift coordinates. Canonical stage identifications are also fixed, since their representatives are the associators specified in def-sf-directed-common-stage-data. Hence any expressions for these arrows using those identifications and inclusion comparisons are preserved term by term. This retains the supplied cone, its finite label and its connecting arrow; it makes no new cone choice.

proof.text: The functor $e$ is additive for the prescribed Hom laws by lem-pur-general-specialization-hom-additivity. Step 3 equips it with the unique prescribed coherent shift comparison, and the forward implication of step 4 says that it carries every distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle. These are exactly the defining conditions for exactness in def-weil-triangulated-category. Therefore $e$ is exact for this comparison.

theorem specialization_commShift_existsUnique :
    ∃! c : (specialization D l hl Ω Y).functor.CommShift ℤ,
      (fun [commInst : (specialization D l hl Ω Y).functor.CommShift ℤ] ↦
        ∀ (n : ℤ) (A : Pair l Ω Y),
          HEq (((specialization D l hl Ω Y).functor.commShiftIso n).hom.app A)
            (𝟙 ((shiftFunctor (SfAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Pair D l hl Ω Y) n).obj
              ((specialization D l hl Ω Y).functor.obj A)))) (commInst := c)
